title: Gene regulation
examples: What is the role of the lac operon in bacteria?
How do transcription factors control gene activity?
Can you explain the process of gene repression?

explain.say: Today we will explore how genes are controlled in living cells. Gene regulation is the process that controls which genes are turned on or off. This process is very important for the cell to function correctly.

items: Cells control which switches are on

explain.say: First we look at the lac operon in bacteria. This system allows bacteria to use lactose only when it is available. It is a classic example of gene control.
The lac operon has specific genes needed to digest lactose. These genes are only switched on when the sugar lactose is present. This saves the cell energy.
Next we discuss transcription factors. These are proteins that bind to DNA to control transcription. They act like molecular switches for the genes.
Transcription factors can either activate or repress gene expression. They either help or block the machinery that reads the gene into RNA.
In real life, your body uses gene regulation constantly. For instance, when you are cold, your body activates genes to generate heat. This is a survival mechanism.

faq.q: What is the difference between operons and gene regulation?
faq.a: An operon is a functional unit of DNA containing a cluster of genes. Gene regulation is the broader process that controls when and how strongly those genes are expressed.
asks: How is an operon different from a gene?
Does operon relate to gene control?

faq.q: Do all organisms use operons for gene control?
faq.a: Operons are a common feature in prokaryotes like bacteria. Eukaryotes, like humans, use more complex mechanisms involving many different types of transcription factors.

faq.q: What is the role of the inducer in the lac operon?
faq.a: The inducer, which is lactose in this case, binds to the repressor protein. This binding changes the shape of the repressor, causing it to fall off the DNA and allowing transcription to begin.
asks: Why does lactose turn the genes on?
What happens when the inducer is present?

faq.q: Can transcription factors work alone to control genes?
faq.a: No, they usually work as a complex. They often require binding to specific DNA sequences and sometimes need other proteins to function correctly.
asks: Do factors need partners to work?
Is one factor enough to start transcription?

faq.q: What happens if the lac operon is permanently switched off?
faq.a: If it is permanently switched off, the bacteria cannot digest lactose. This would severely limit its ability to grow in an environment containing that sugar.
asks: What if the genes are always off?
Why is lactose important for the bacteria?

facts: The lac operon allows bacteria to metabolize lactose efficiently.
Transcription factors are proteins that bind to DNA to control gene expression.
Activator proteins increase the rate of transcription.
Repressor proteins block the transcription process when unnecessary.

quiz.say: If lactose is present, what happens to the lac operon genes?

options.show: The repressor binds tighter to the DNA
options.say: The repressor binds tighter to the DNA

options.show: The bacteria stop using all energy
options.say: The bacteria stop using all energy

quiz.why: The presence of lactose acts as an inducer, removing the block and allowing transcription to proceed.

wrong.0: This suggests the genes are destroyed, but the process is about controlling reading, not destruction.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because the inducer causes the repressor to detach from the DNA.
wrong.2: While energy is conserved, the immediate result is the activation of the necessary genes, not a total stop.

quiz.say: A protein that binds to DNA and increases transcription is called a:
quiz.why: Activator proteins are specifically named for their function of promoting or increasing gene transcription rates.

wrong.1: Repressors do the opposite; they decrease or block transcription.
wrong.2: Inducers are the small molecules that trigger the change, not the protein that binds to the DNA.
wrong.3: Operon describes the group of genes, not the specific protein that controls them.

quiz.say: If the cell lacks lactose, the lac operon genes are best described as:
quiz.why: Without the inducer, the repressor protein remains bound to the operator, blocking RNA polymerase.

wrong.0: The control mechanism is based on nutrient availability, not the time of day.
wrong.2: This would waste energy producing enzymes that are not needed in the absence of lactose.
wrong.3: Gene expression in bacteria is highly controlled, not random.
